answers.cut_pace: Steady: about 0.5% of my weight a week
answers.target: Lose the belly and see some abs
answers.why_now: Holiday booked, and I've let things slip since starting a desk job last year.
answers.holding_back: No real plan. I go to the gym and do whatever I feel like, then eat badly in the evenings.
answers.routine: Bro split: chest Monday, back Wednesday, arms Friday. Skip legs a lot.
answers.lifts: Bench 90 kg × 5, squat 110 kg × 5, lat pulldown 70 kg × 10
answers.injuries: Lower back gets tight after deadlifts. Fine otherwise.
answers.normal_day: Skip breakfast, meal deal at lunch, pasta or a takeaway for tea, crisps and chocolate in the evening.
answers.food_style: Mostly whole foods, plus protein powder
answers.anything_else: Away on a stag do 14 to 16 March.
answers.likes: Chicken, steak, rice, pasta, curry, eggs, Greek yoghurt

training.title: Upper / lower, 4 days
training.summary: Four 60-minute sessions. Chest and back get extra work, legs come back in gently, and nothing loads your lower back the way deadlifts do.
training.schedule: Mon lower, Tue upper, Wed football, Thu upper, Fri lower
training.effort: Weeks 1 and 2: stop every set with 2 to 3 reps left. From week 3: 1 to 2 reps left on the big lifts, and take the last set of the smaller exercises close to failure.
training.progression: When you hit the top of the rep range on every set, add the smallest weight jump next time. Log every set so your coach can see it.

exercises.name: Hack squat
exercises.notes: Leg press if it's taken. Weeks 1 and 2: 2 sets.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.notes: Lower until your knees reach 90°. Weeks 1 and 2: 2 sets.

exercises.name: Standing calf raise
exercises.notes: Pause for a second at the bottom.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.notes: 2 lighter warm-up sets first. Start around 80 kg for 6 and build back past 90 × 5.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.notes: Once you get 10 on every set, add weight with a belt.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.notes: Chest on the pad, so your lower back stays out of it.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.notes: Start around 60 kg and build back to 70 × 10 and beyond.

exercises.name: Incline machine press
exercises.notes: Smith machine incline press if there's no machine.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.notes: Sit tall. Don't rock back to move the weight.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
exercises.notes: Barbell or machine. Squeeze at the top and keep your ribs down.

exercises.name: Dumbbell split squat
exercises.notes: Weeks 1 and 2: bodyweight or light dumbbells, 2 sets.

notes: Wednesday is football. That's your cardio for the day, and legs are trained Monday and Friday so they're fresh for it.
No deadlifts or back extensions for now. Say in your check-in how your lower back feels. If it's happy after 4 weeks, your coach may add Romanian deadlifts.
Walking and cycling both count towards your steps. Aim for 8,000 to 10,000 a day.
Machine taken? Use the closest swap and write it in your log.

nutrition.title: Steady cut, 4 meals
nutrition.summary: About 300 kcal under what you eat now, plus a few more steps. That's roughly 0.3 to 0.5 kg a week, which gets you to 80 kg well before Spain without starving you.

meals.name: Lunch, 12 to 1pm: chicken, rice and veg box

items.food: Porridge oats (stir in raw, or soak overnight)
5% beef mince (cook the 500 g pack as 4 portions)
0% Greek style yoghurt, stirred in at the end

meals.name: Evening, instead of crisps and chocolate

items.food: Your whey protein, in the milk

supplements.name: Whey protein (the tub you already have)
supplements.why: About 24 g protein with no cooking. When it runs out, any whey with 20 g+ protein a scoop is fine; online tubs are usually cheaper than Tesco's.

shopping.item: Large chicken breast fillet pack, 1.6 kg
Lean beef steak mince 5% fat, 500 g
Sweet chilli and garlic sauce, 250 ml

shopping.note: (only if you don't have oil; lasts about 6 weeks)

swaps: Busy day, meal deal instead of the lunch box: a chicken or protein sandwich or wrap (25 g+ protein), a protein yoghurt or milk drink, and fruit instead of crisps. Aim for 550 to 650 kcal.
Chicken ↔ lean steak or turkey mince (same weight)
Rice ↔ pasta (same dry weight) or potatoes (3× the weight)
Peanut butter on toast ↔ 2 eggs on toast
Greek yoghurt ↔ skyr or a high-protein yoghurt pot
Shopping at Aldi Witney instead: the same list works with Aldi's own version of each item.
notes: 1 free night a week: takeaway, a meal out or drinks. Keep lunch, the 4pm snack and the shake as normal, and pick something with plenty of protein. A pint is about 200 kcal.
This list is about £43 (£37 if you already have oil). Rice, pasta, oats and the jars last 2 to 3 weeks, so most weeks after are about £33.
Batch cook twice a week (Sunday and Wednesday). Keep 2 days of boxes in the fridge and freeze the rest; move tomorrow's box to the fridge the night before.
Weigh yourself most mornings, after the toilet and before food. We go by the weekly average, not single days.
Steps: aim for 8,000 to 10,000 a day. A 20-minute walk at lunch covers most of the gap.
Christmas week: eat around 2,700 kcal, keep protein high, keep walking. Back to the plan after Boxing Day. Your coach will remind you nearer the time.

whyTraining.point: Upper / lower, 4 days (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri)
whyTraining.why: He picked those 4 days and 60 minutes. His bro split hits each muscle once a week, and he skips legs.
whyTraining.effect: Every muscle is trained twice a week, which holds muscle better on a cut. Legs are half the plan, so they can't be skipped.
Two days between leg sessions and football, so he isn't sore for the game or hurt by it.

whyTraining.point: No deadlifts: hip thrusts and leg curls instead
whyTraining.why: His lower back gets tight after deadlifts and he won't do them (flagged as an injury).
whyTraining.effect: Glutes and hamstrings still get hard work with nothing heavy on his lower back. Look again at Romanian deadlifts after 4 weeks if his back is fine.

whyTraining.point: Hack squat and leg press, not barbell squats (for now)
whyTraining.why: He's barely trained legs lately, and a heavy back squat loads the same lower back.
whyTraining.effect: Legs get pushed hard with less risk while they come back. Barbell squats can return later if he wants them.

whyTraining.point: Extra chest and back: 14 sets each a week
whyTraining.why: He picked chest and back as priorities and loves bench and pull-ups.
whyTraining.effect: More work where he wants results, and his favourite lifts open each upper day, so he enjoys going.

whyTraining.point: Easier first 2 weeks (2 to 3 reps left, fewer leg sets)
whyTraining.why: He trains on and off and hasn't done proper leg work in a while.
whyTraining.effect: Less soreness, so he doesn't miss sessions or football in the first fortnight.

whyFood.why: He eats about 2,700 and his weight is flat. The formula guess (2,990 to 3,170) is within 15% of that, so his own number wins. He picked the steady pace.
whyFood.effect: About 300 kcal under maintenance plus more steps: roughly 0.3 to 0.5 kg a week. He only needs 0.27 kg a week to reach 80 kg by 20 June, so Christmas and the stag do won't sink it.

whyFood.why: He eats about 110 g now. He's carrying extra fat, so protein is set from his 80 kg goal weight (2 g per kg).
whyFood.effect: Keeps his muscle while he loses fat, and keeps him fuller on fewer calories.

whyFood.why: He skips breakfast and asked for 4 meals a day.
whyFood.effect: No change to his mornings. The food lands in the afternoon and evening, when he's actually hungry and training.

whyFood.point: Evening shake, toast and 20 g dark chocolate
whyFood.why: His evenings are crisps and chocolate, which is where the plan would break.
whyFood.effect: He still gets something sweet at night, but with about 50 g of protein instead of none.

whyFood.point: Tesco list, mostly Aldi Price Match items
whyFood.why: He shops at Tesco Extra Kidlington and Aldi Witney, with a £40 to £60 budget and basic cooking.
whyFood.effect: One shop, at Aldi prices: about £37 the first week (plus £5.25 if he needs oil), then about £33. That leaves room for his free night.

whyFood.why: He eats out or gets a takeaway 1 to 2 times a week and has 1 to 5 drinks.
whyFood.effect: The plan already allows for it, so one night out doesn't feel like failing.

whyFood.point: Only his own whey, no other supplements
whyFood.why: He said he only wants protein powder.
whyFood.effect: No extra cost, and nothing he didn't ask for.
